title: analyze: mid-run re-anchor halt when unbound cuts outnumber cuts bound to the Question
description:
A mid-run re-anchor in /analyze, the in-flight complement to the front gate. At each stage boundary, count execution_order steps and probes that bind to the pre-registered comparison or to a candidate Claim, against those that bind to nothing. When the unbound outnumber the bound (threshold to be set from the retro), halt with needs_attention naming each unbound cut and asking the Operator whether it serves the Question, is a dead_end, or is a reframe. Never delete a cut; the halt only asks for its kind.

This is the mechanism for "the analyst got lost in the weeds and missed the point", the gap named in the 2026-09-16 review, and for Vera's "stop early and optimistically" from the other side (a run with many cuts and no bound Claim is the same symptom). Blocked on the retro because the retro tells us whether probes alone were enough to see this, and what the honest threshold is.

title: Run Issue requests reliably with clear pause and retry states
description: Implement `aftergrid intake` as the v0 runner for an Operator's Instance; internal aftergrid development still uses beads. Poll labelled GitHub Issues, snapshot the request, establish a stable run identity, invoke the headless harness with the configured hook/limits, and create or update one linked Finding PR. Treat issue content and source values as task data, not permission to alter controls. Missing definitions, external sign-off or clarification pauses as needs-input; technical failure reports a recoverable reason. Retry/resume must neither duplicate PRs nor lose completed artifacts, and concurrent duplicate triggers claim the same run safely. Human approval remains required for publication. A GitHub Actions recipe is optional; it must not be necessary for the local poller to work.

- [ ] Issue edits after dispatch are detected as a new input revision or require explicit resume; partial work cannot be mislabeled complete.
- [ ] Messages/logs contain ids and actionable status without private query results or credentials; publication never occurs on agent review alone.

title: Table docs and join heuristics mined into proposed context, approved by the Operator
description:
Source: docs/inputs/research-notes-2026-09-16.md and -17.md. Every source names context as the accuracy lever:
Meta calls personal query history the "killer feature" ("an AI agent without personalized context is just a chatbot
with database access"); Vera's harness beat Claude Code 73% to 48% on the same model because of a catalog of
modeled tables and join heuristics; Anthropic's accuracy went 21% -> 95% with a semantic layer. aftergrid has
approved Metric definitions and readers.md, and no table/join layer and no learning loop. This is the largest
product risk after v0: strongest at the decision step, weakest at what every source says decides accuracy.

Post-v0 (v0.1 or later). Do:
- `aftergrid setup` (or a new `aftergrid learn`) mines what the adapter can see: information_schema, and where
  available query history (Snowflake QUERY_HISTORY, BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS, Postgres pg_stat_statements,
  DuckDB none) into PROPOSED table docs: description, columns used, common joins and filters, freshness. Same gate
  as ADR 0007: proposed until an Operator approves; the agent reads approved docs first and proposed docs only with
  the status shown.
- Corrections: when a review or the Operator corrects a table choice, join or filter during an Analysis, the skill
  writes a proposed edit to the table doc (Anthropic's correction harvesting; Meta's Memories) instead of learning
  silently.
- Everything stays Instance-side (ADR 0002). Never a personal-history "clone a colleague" feature: provenance per
  doc, owner per doc.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Contract for table docs (docs/contracts/instance-layout.md) with proposed/approved lifecycle and content hash,
  mirroring definitions.
- [ ] setup produces proposed docs from the fixture DuckDB schema; a Snowflake or BigQuery history path is specified
  even if not implemented.
- [ ] A golden Question that needs a join heuristic passes with approved docs and abstains without them.

title: Counter-metric on a Metric definition, reported by any Finding it heads
description:
Owner decision 2026-09-17 (docs/inputs/research-notes-2026-09-17.md): the Goodhart gap is closed in v0. Nothing in
the Engine notices when an approved Metric definition has become a target. A Metric definition may name a
counter-metric, and a Finding whose published decision metric names one must report it.

Sketch, to be settled in the contract before code:
- Definition front matter gains optional `counter_metrics: [{ id, version?, why }]`, each naming another definition
  in the same Instance. `why` is one plain sentence: what gaming the primary metric would do to this one.
- Optional and omitted-when-empty, so the definition content hash (instance-layout.md) of every already-approved
  definition is unchanged. Adding the field to an approved definition changes its hash and needs a new version and
  a new Operator approval, which is the correct behaviour: naming the counter-metric is part of the meaning.
- `proposeDefinition` (src/analysis/definitions.ts) accepts and renders the field; `/grill-question` asks for it when
  it proposes a decision metric ("what would get worse if this were pushed hard?") and accepts "none, because …".
- New Check in the publication path (scripts/lib/validate-finding.mjs beside definition_not_approved): when the
  decision metric's definition lists counter-metrics, the Finding carries at least one traced value per
  counter-metric over the same population and window, or an explicit stated reason it could not be computed.
  A counter-metric may be a proposed definition or a Diagnostic calculation; it is never the headline.
- The Engine reports the counter-metric; it never judges the trade. Same rule as Decisions (ADR 0009).
- `/write-finding` memo template: counter-metric values sit with the evidence for the headline Claim, not in caveats.
- Revisit (v0.1) rechecks them like any other Claim; no v0 work.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] instance-layout.md, checks-and-results.md and memo-template.md specify the field, the Check, its category and
the memo placement; CONTEXT.md gains **Counter-metric** with its _Avoid_ list; ADR 0007 amended or a new ADR.
- [ ] Fixture Instance: one approved definition gains a counter-metric through a version bump with a recomputed
approval hash; the other fixture and nyc-open-data definitions keep their existing hashes byte for byte.
- [ ] Negative fixtures: decision metric with a counter-metric and no reported value fails with the new category;
a stated could-not-compute reason passes; a counter-metric id that does not resolve fails.
- [ ] A definition with no counter_metrics publishes exactly as today.
- [ ] `/grill-question` and `/write-finding` prose updated; skill evals cover the prompt and the "none, because" path.

title: Bind publication to verified human approval and exact evidence
description: Implement the publication boundary separately from evidence validity. title: CLI scaffold, new Finding drafts, and contract validation
description: Implement the reviewed contract, not a second competing schema. Create the repository layout, TypeScript CLI, test harness and `aftergrid new finding <slug>`. New creates fresh identifiers and an explicitly incomplete draft without overwriting an existing Finding. `aftergrid check` separates syntactic/schema errors, incomplete content, evidence validity and publication readiness, returning stable machine-readable categories plus useful human explanations and locations. Initial fixtures drive schema/reference behavior; execution and publication gates are completed by their downstream beads. An untouched draft may be structurally valid but cannot claim a complete or reviewed analysis. Use a supported Node/platform matrix and packaged dependencies that install without a local compiler; this does not prohibit prebuilt native runtime packages.

- [ ] Both completed exemplars pass implemented schema/reference checks; unresolved references, missing/duplicate row keys and invalid identifier grammar fail with precise locations and categories.

- [ ] Seam-1 checks run in CI; CLI help states the supported runtime and draft/check/render lifecycle; local install needs no native compilation on the declared supported platforms.
- [ ] Artifact-verification and retained-input rerun modes report whether SQL was actually reexecuted; a saved artifact is never labeled freshly rechecked merely because its hashes match.

title: Deterministic learning and failure dataset with reference Questions
description: Generate a small synthetic consumer-app dataset for both engineering fixtures and model evaluation, using supported DuckDB runtime facilities. Users, events and subscriptions contain planted churn/funnel/mix effects plus deliberately labeled duplicates, zero denominators, late events, incomplete coverage and insufficient evidence. Produce three to five reference Questions with approved synthetic definitions, expected answers or abstention, tolerances and expected evidence constraints. Keep deterministic engine errors distinct from semantic situations an honest analysis must explain: population mix shift does not by itself require a mechanical Check failure. Nightly orchestration lives in its own bead. These fixtures should help explain why an answer is supported, not reward a model for repeating a predetermined recommendation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A seed recreates the same logical rows/results and input metadata; any byte-hash expectations define canonical storage/serialization rather than relying on incidental database bytes.
- [ ] Every planted failure has an expected engine category, analytical outcome or review concern, clearly distinguishing those layers.
- [ ] Reference Questions and definitions validate; at least one expects abstention and one tests denominator/baseline reasoning.
- [ ] Reference calculations are independently inspectable SQL/data examples with units, population, windows and tolerances; expected causal conclusions are not invented from associations.
- [ ] Fixtures contain no Spot Sports identifiers, schema or production data and run in bounded CI resources.

title: eval: tier 3 depth — score a run against a shallow baseline for the same Question
description:
DoorDash's Vera names the tier 3 failure: models "stop early and optimistically" and return "superficial, albeit plausible, answers without diving deeper." Nobody has an eval for it; DoorDash lists it as open. aftergrid measures Reader comprehension, not depth.

Design an eval that scores depth against a shallow baseline for the same Question: does the run name a denominator, a comparison, a window and a material caveat; does it record at least one dead end; does its answer-bearing Claim rest on the pre-registered comparison rather than a post-hoc cut; does it say what it could not verify. Deterministic scorers where possible, an LLM judge only for the rest, following the pattern in src/eval/ and the nightly eval (ag-nightly-eval-0dv). The video-podcast baselines and Finding are the first data point; the nyc-open-data Findings the second.

Blocked on the hands-on retro on purpose: the run tells us which of those signals actually separated deep from shallow.

description: Finish the internal v0 milestone only after every retained v0 feature has implemented acceptance evidence. Verify the exact candidate revision with deterministic Finding/adapter suites, a green full golden evaluation, complete private automated readout, actual Reader smoke feedback, package/install smoke and truthful capability matrix. Check publication binding, setup/hook and asynchronous intake explicitly; parent-child membership alone is not sufficient dependency coverage. Record outstanding usability/operational limitations and the next external-release study. This task does not publish packages, flip repository visibility or claim external-release validation merely because a study is scheduled. Follow-on release readiness has its own bead; Revisit runtime remains v0.1.

- [ ] All v0 child feature tasks are in the milestone blocking-dependency closure and completed with their named evidence; deferred Revisit runtime is excluded.
- [ ] Deterministic seams and full golden suite pass at the exact recorded candidate SHA, with no stale green substituted.
- [ ] Private real Finding and Reader smoke show answer, denominator, baseline, limitation, action/inaction and follow-up understanding.
- [ ] Complete clean-install workflow, publication authority, hook and asynchronous intake acceptance evidence are linked.

title: v0: one Finding end to end
description: Deliver the owner-approved v0 through reviewed exemplars, one retained DuckDB Finding, evidence and publication validation, a manual private Reader pilot, the full craft/analysis skill chain, deterministic decisions, both adapters, setup/hook, background intake, distribution smoke and versioned evaluations. Sources: docs/spec/v0-one-finding-end-to-end.md, docs/design/v0-design-2026-09-15.md, CONTEXT.md, ADRs 0001–0009 and docs/design/bead-plan-review-2026-09-15.md. Beads are the development tracker; GitHub Issues remain the product Instance intake. Scope is preserved; Revisit runtime and external release readiness are separate follow-ons. Internal milestone completion does not authorize public activation.
design: Order: exemplars plus real Reader feedback -> skeleton -> DuckDB; renderer, Recheck validation and synthetic references -> evidence validation -> manual private Finding before skill work. Writer and question/analysis skills can then develop independently; iteration uses renderer plus publication binding; orchestrator consumes those tested contracts. Postgres and hook work can run after DuckDB; setup integrates both plus approval preflight. Intake requires setup and orchestrator. Decide has its own deterministic command ticket after evidence/schema. Automated real readout compares with the manual pilot, records a real decision and genuine approval. Distribution tests the complete install without publishing. Nightly evaluation is separate from fixture generation; the internal milestone requires every v0 feature transitively. External-release study/readiness and v0.1 Revisit depend on that milestone, not vice versa. Every bead names observable acceptance evidence; user studies require real people, never simulated completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every retained v0 child feature is covered by the internal milestone dependency closure and passes named acceptance evidence.
- [ ] The exact candidate revision passes Finding/adapter seams and the full golden suite; required human Reader and owner-decision evidence is recorded privately.
- [ ] A complete locally packed install supports all promoted skills and v0 commands, including hook and intake, with honest capability/readiness status.
- [ ] Private production data never enters the Engine; external-release study and public activation remain explicit follow-on gates.

title: Record an owner decision against reviewed evidence
description: Implement aftergrid decide as a deterministic user action, separate from evidence lint and narrative revision. Validate owner-supplied action or deliberate inaction, rationale, date, exact Finding revision and Claim ids, revisit condition and optional outcome. Show the proposed record before confirmation or accept explicit complete CLI input; never infer approval or a decision from a merged Finding. Append durably with a stable record id, avoid duplicates on retry and preserve prior decisions when corrections create a new linked record. A missing outcome means pending, not zero impact. The Reader follow-up route reaches the Operator, who records the actual owner decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Valid explicit input creates one Decision record bound to existing Finding/Claim revisions; invalid/missing references or owner fields fail without a partial append.
- [ ] Action and deliberate inaction both work; rationale and revisit condition are preserved and unknown outcomes remain pending.
- [ ] Retry with the same request id produces no duplicate; a conflicting reuse or concurrent append is handled explicitly without losing records.
- [ ] Correction appends a linked superseding record, preserving the prior record; merge or render alone never creates a decision.
- [ ] CLI output shows what was recorded and where the owner can find it; test uses synthetic records and includes malformed dates/timezones.

title: Video-podcast Finding on the recorded path: the hands-on run
description:
The first real Finding on the recorded path (ADR 0010): the Operator's harness runs every query, aftergrid records what ran, no adapter. Scope, decisions and start-here list: docs/design/hands-on-scope-2026-09-16.md. Research behind it: docs/inputs/research-notes-2026-09-16.md (Vera, Confidence, DANA).

Verbatim ask (Operator, 2026-09-16): "We want to do an analysis on Video Podcasts and try to get an understanding on how they correlate to Apple Podcast rankings (our source for podcast_rankings)."

Settled by the owner: the Reader is a podcaster and the Finding is PUBLIC; the Spot Sports Instance is scaffolded by hand; the middle of the analysis is recorded in analysis.yaml#/probes (kinds landed in ag-3ce); the self-serve baseline is best of three. Positioning under test: "go deeper when the agent can't" / "beyond self-serve".

Two things are measured at once: (1) does the skills chain go visibly deeper than a plain self-serve answer, judged by a podcaster in the reader-session protocol; (2) does the Finding contract hold with nothing captured or rerun. A run that shows the contract needs revision is a valid outcome.

Reference run: examples/nyc-open-data has two Findings produced by /analyze in a real Claude Code session on the adapter path (ag-demo-open-data-qsl.5/.6). This epic is the recorded-path counterpart on private data.

Hard rule: no Spot Sports schema, metric, id or credential enters this repository. Everything Instance-side lives in spot_sports/analytics/.

Unresolved owner questions (ask before the step that needs them): which podcaster runs the Reader session and is their show in the ranking source; is the Finding published as Spot Sports, with the ranking source named as Apple charts or Spot's derived ranking; is the Operator the sole trusted approver; does the internal second Finding get scoped now or after.

title: hands-on: scaffold the Spot Sports Instance by hand (podcaster Reader, public export policy, no adapter)
description:
Create spot_sports/analytics/ by hand following docs/contracts/instance-layout.md. Do NOT run aftergrid setup; the point is to learn what a hand scaffold needs that setup would not have produced, and to record that list in the retro bead.

Must contain: aftergrid.yaml with NO connection.adapter (recorded route; see docs/contracts/record.md and the recorded exemplar fixtures/instance/analytics/findings/2026-09-16-price-change-cancellations-recorded); readers.md with a `podcaster` profile (makes decisions about their own show, does not write SQL, reads on a phone, is not a Spot Sports employee, will share the document with other podcasters); a PUBLIC export policy per docs/contracts/publication.md (reader-safe projection only; nothing about ranking pipeline mechanics or unpublished product bets); an empty definitions/ (the grill proposes them); an empty decisions/ log; findings/.

Publication policy needs a repository, an automation login and a trusted approver; the owner has not said whether they are the sole approver. Ask, do not assume.

Done when `aftergrid check` on a throwaway `new finding` in this Instance reports no schema error and no instance-layout error, and a short list "what setup would have missed" is written into the Instance README for the retro.

title: hands-on: three self-serve baselines on the verbatim ask, verbatim, best of three with reason
description:
Three plain Claude Code sessions, no aftergrid skills loaded, the same data tools the skills run will use (the Operator's Supabase Postgres access and the PostHog MCP). Ask the verbatim question from the epic each time, one turn, no coaching. Save each answer verbatim (including any SQL and tables) under spot_sports/analytics/findings/<slug>/baseline/{1,2,3}.md with the session date and the model.

Choose the best one to carry into the reader session by the Operator's judgement and write why in baseline/README.md. This is the self-serve answer the Finding is compared against. Record wall-clock time per session.

Expected: a plausible table and a sentence about correlation, no denominator, no window, no statement of what it could not verify. If a baseline is better than that, say so; the comparison is only useful if it is honest.

title: hands-on: /grill-question on the verbatim ask; podcaster decision, proposed definitions, falsifier or needs_reframing
description:
Run /grill-question on the verbatim ask in the hand-scaffolded Instance (aftergrid new finding <slug> --ask "<verbatim>" --reader podcaster). Follow skills/checked-analysis/references/clarification.md; record clarified_at.

Expect the hard parts to be: the DECISION (the podcaster's: whether adding video to their show is associated with ranking well enough to be worth the cost; the internal ranking-weight decision is a different Reader and therefore a different Finding, see the deferred bead); the METRIC (there is no approved definition of "video podcast" or of "ranking position", both get proposed as lifecycle: proposed with counter-metrics per ag-counter-metric-fv0); the COMPARISON (video vs non-video shows within a sport? within a rank band? over which snapshot batches?); the FALSIFIER (must be a runnable Check on the recorded path).

An ask phrased as "correlate" may legitimately end as question.state: not_answerable -> outcome needs_reframing. That is a result, not a failure. An associational Claim published to podcasters must be typed associational and must not read as causal.

Done when aftergrid check reports the intended state with no schema error, and the hand-on summary (step 5 of the skill) names every proposed definition and everything unresolved with its owner.

title: hands-on: /analyze on the recorded path; probes kept as they happen; run-log of adapter assumptions
description:
Run /analyze on the Finding from the grill bead, on the recorded path: the harness runs every query and Check through its own tool, `aftergrid record` pins each with --tool named as the Operator says it. No capture, no adapter. snapshot.guarantees ends as [artifact_replay].

Keep analysis.yaml#/probes as it happens: at, kind (exploratory | dead_end | reframe), question, observed, changed_plan. Dead ends are recorded, never deleted. This list is the primary evidence for the retro on the middle of the analysis.

Also log, in the Finding directory (run-log.md): every point where a skill or contract still assumed aftergrid runs the SQL and the Operator had to do something else; wall-clock per stage from analysis-progress.yaml; every halt and why. Normal completion is an evidence-valid draft reviewed by agents, awaiting human publication readiness; do not describe it as verified or approved.

Done when `aftergrid check` reports evidence valid and the three reviews current, or the run has halted with a precise reason recorded in analysis-progress.yaml.

title: hands-on: reader session with a podcaster on baseline vs Finding, plus the share question
description:
Run docs/design/reader-session-a2f.md with ONE podcaster who does not write SQL, on a phone, on both artifacts: the chosen baseline first, then the rendered Finding (draft render is fine; label it draft). Add one question to the protocol for this run: "Would you share this with another podcaster? What would you say it shows?"

Owner question to settle first: which podcaster, and is their show in the ranking source (a show in the data makes the denominator question concrete; a show outside it tests whether the Finding travels).

Record observations verbatim and sanitized into the Observations section of reader-session-a2f.md, one block per artifact. Pass criteria are in that file. Also record whether the contact route on the Finding works for someone with no GitHub and no mail client, because this Finding will be public.

A session that shows the Finding is no clearer than the baseline is a valid and important outcome. Write it down.

title: hands-on: first real public publication path (export policy, human APPROVED, render for publication)
description:
First real run of the public publication path on the recorded route. Needs, in order: the export policy in the Instance set to public with the reader-safe projection; the rendered Finding checked by a human for anything that should not be public (ranking pipeline mechanics, unpublished product bets, internal ids); a PR in spot_sports carrying the Finding; a human APPROVED review at the analyzed commit by an allowlisted approver; `aftergrid check` reporting publication ready as a separate fact from evidence valid; `aftergrid render` for publication succeeding only then.

Owner questions to settle before rendering: is the Finding published as Spot Sports; is the ranking source described as "Apple Podcasts charts" or as Spot's own ranking derived from them; who is the trusted approver.

Record every place the publication contract (docs/contracts/publication.md) or render refused, was unclear, or let something through it should not have. Those become beads. Do not work around a refusal to get the Finding out; the refusal is the data.

title: hands-on: retro on the middle of the analysis and the recorded path; opens the follow-up beads
description:
Write docs/design/hands-on-retro-<date>.md answering the learn criteria in the scope doc: did the skills go deeper than the baseline in a way the Reader could see (cite the reader session); where did the recorded path break the contract (cite run-log.md); what did the Operator need mid-analysis that no skill provided.

Specifically on the middle: was analysis.yaml#/probes, kept honestly, enough to see afterwards where the analysis went and why? If not, what could the list not hold (branching hypotheses, sub-questions, parked cuts, a re-anchor to the Question)? The shape of whatever replaces or extends it comes from that answer, not from a design in advance.

Also fold in: the "what setup would have missed" list from the scaffold bead; time per stage; every publication refusal.

Close by opening beads for each concrete finding and listing them in the retro. The 2026-09-16 review's follow-up beads (tier 3 depth eval, diagnosing-metric-change, analyze re-anchor halt, Instance catalog) are blocked on this retro on purpose: the scope doc says anything the run reveals becomes a bead, not a pre-emptive fix.

title: Write Findings people can understand and inspect
description: Implement /write-finding and /shape-narrative under writing-for-agents, using lessons from the manual Reader pilot. Consume the shared Analysis-directory contract and produce fixed sections, typed Claims/Recheck policies, evidence references, chart specs and a valid manifest. Select the named Reader profile or clearly disclosed generic fallback. Put material caveats beside the Answer; require chart/table evidence only for numeric Claims. Questions requiring reframing and insufficient evidence are honest valid outcomes. The writer cannot fabricate definitions, approvals, evidence or a causal conclusion to satisfy the template. Use synthetic recorded runs as regression fixtures and named qualitative reviewer criteria; do not embed company nouns or personal Reader details in Engine skills.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Numeric and nonnumeric Analysis inputs produce evidence-valid Findings with zero manual structural/value corrections in the recorded acceptance run.
- [ ] Answer-first structure and Claim evidence lint pass; method/narrative criteria explicitly cover what lint cannot judge.
- [ ] A named Reader profile and missing-profile fallback are both exercised; denominator, baseline, window and decision-changing caveat remain understandable.
- [ ] All displayed analytical values bind to the input evidence, with no invented causal wording or approval status.
- [ ] Recorded synthetic runs preserve inputs, model/skill versions, outputs and reviewer outcome; private pilot observations are not committed.
